Sequence Regression Tree Plot

Source: R/ggseqtreeplot.R
ggseqtreeplot.Rd

Function for rendering regression trees of sequences (obtained with TraMineR::seqtree) with ggplot2 (Wickham 2016) . The function re-produces the tree plots rendered with TraMineR::seqtreedisplay (Gabadinho et al. 2011; Studer et al. 2011) without requiring an installation of 'GraphViz'. Each node of the tree is displayed as a sequence plot produced by one of the ggseq*plot functions of this package.

Usage

ggseqtreeplot(
  tree,
  seqdata = NULL,
  type = "d",
  only.leaf = FALSE,
  with.legend = TRUE,
  with.quality = TRUE,
  quality.multiline = FALSE,
  title.size = 9,
  label.width = 30,
  common.y = FALSE,
  node.layers = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

tree

A regression tree of sequences (class seqtree) created with TraMineR::seqtree. Trees of class disstree (TraMineR::disstree) can be used if seqdata is specified.

seqdata

State sequence object (class stslist) created with the TraMineR::seqdef function. If NULL (default) the sequence object stored in the tree object is used.

type

Type of the sequence plot shown in the nodes of the tree: "d" for state distribution plots (default, ggseqdplot), "i" for index plots (ggseqiplot), "f" for sequence frequency plots (ggseqfplot), "ms" for modal state plots (ggseqmsplot), or "mt" for mean time plots (ggseqmtplot).

only.leaf

If TRUE sequence plots are only shown for the terminal nodes (leaves) of the tree; the inner nodes are shown as text boxes. Default is FALSE.

with.legend

Specifies if a legend of the states is shown (default is TRUE)

with.quality

Specifies if the global quality measures of the tree (Pseudo F, Pseudo R2, and Levene statistic) are shown below the tree (default is TRUE). The measures are rendered as plot tag and can be moved (see Details).

quality.multiline

If TRUE the global quality measures are printed in separate lines instead of one line, which is useful if they are placed next to the root node (default is FALSE).

title.size

Font size of the node titles (split condition, n, s2, and next split variable); default is 9. Smaller values might be required for large trees.

label.width

Maximum number of characters per line for the split labels. Longer labels (e.g., splits over sets of factor levels) are wrapped. Default is 30.

common.y

If TRUE all node plots share the same y-axis range, which eases the comparison of the nodes. Only used for mean time plots (type = "mt"); the y-axes of state distribution plots and modal state plots always range from 0 to 1. Default is FALSE.

node.layers

A ggplot component (e.g., a scale or a theme) or a list of ggplot components that is added to each of the node plots, e.g., list(scale_x_discrete(labels = ...), theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 6))). The components are added after the default layout of the node plots and therefore overwrite it. Default is NULL.

...

additional arguments passed on to the plot function specified with type (e.g. border = TRUE or sortv = "from.start" for index plots). If sortv is a vector (of the same length as the sequence data), it is subsetted for each node.

Value

A tree plot created by using ggplot2. If stored as object the resulting list object (of class gg and ggplot) also contains the data describing the nodes of the tree (position, label, n, discrepancy, split variable, and the indices of the cases in each node).

Details

The function walks through the tree object generated by TraMineR::seqtree and stores the information of each node in a data frame. Like in TraMineR::seqtreedisplay each node shows the split condition (or "Root"), the number of (weighted) cases (n), the discrepancy of the sequences within the node (s2), and – for inner nodes – the variable used for the next split along with its R2.

The positions of the nodes are computed with a simple algorithm: the terminal nodes (leaves) are placed next to each other from left to right, and every inner node is centered above its two child nodes. The vertical position reflects the depth of a node.

For each node a sequence plot is generated by calling the function specified with type on the respective subset of the sequence data. The resulting plots are placed on an empty plot ("canvas") using ggplot2::annotation_custom. The edges of the tree are drawn with ggplot2::geom_segment. Axis titles and legends of the node plots are removed. Instead, a common legend for the whole tree is shown at the bottom of the plot.

Note that the node plots are drawn as images on the canvas. Therefore, the appearance of the node plots cannot be changed afterwards using +. Instead, scales, themes, or other ggplot components that should be applied to all node plots can be specified with the node.layers argument. The overall plot (title, legend, ...), however, can be adjusted just like any other ggplot (e.g., + labs(title = "My tree")). The global quality measures are rendered as plot tag. Their position can be changed with theme(plot.tag.position = ..., plot.tag.location = "panel") (see examples). The legend can be moved with theme(legend.position = ...) and rearranged with guides(fill = guide_legend(...)). For large trees, it is recommended to save the plot with a large size, e.g. by using ggplot2::ggsave with appropriate width and height values.

References

Gabadinho A, Ritschard G, Müller NS, Studer M (2011). “Analyzing and Visualizing State Sequences in R with TraMineR.” Journal of Statistical Software, 40(4), 1–37. doi:10.18637/jss.v040.i04 .

Studer M, Ritschard G, Gabadinho A, Müller NS (2011). “Discrepancy Analysis of State Sequences.” Sociological Methods & Research, 40(3), 471–510. doi:10.1177/0049124111415372 .

Wickham H (2016). ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis, Use R!, 2nd ed. edition. Springer, Cham. doi:10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4 .

Examples

library(TraMineR)
library(ggplot2)

# Use example data from TraMineR: mvad data set
data(mvad)

# We use only a sample of 300 cases
set.seed(1)
mvad <- mvad[sample(nrow(mvad), 300), ]
mvad.seq <- seqdef(mvad[, 17:86], xtstep = 6)
#>  [>] 6 distinct states appear in the data: 
#>      1 = FE
#>      2 = HE
#>      3 = employment
#>      4 = joblessness
#>      5 = school
#>      6 = training
#>  [>] state coding:
#>        [alphabet]  [label]     [long label] 
#>      1  FE          FE          FE
#>      2  HE          HE          HE
#>      3  employment  employment  employment
#>      4  joblessness joblessness joblessness
#>      5  school      school      school
#>      6  training    training    training
#>  [>] 300 sequences in the data set
#>  [>] min/max sequence length: 70/70

# Compute dissimilarities and grow the regression tree
mvad.diss <- seqdist(mvad.seq, method = "HAM")
#>  [>] 300 sequences with 6 distinct states
#>  [>] creating a 'sm' with a single substitution cost of 1
#>  [>] creating 6x6 substitution-cost matrix using 1 as constant value
#>  [>] checking 'sm' (size and triangle inequality)
#>  [>] 227 distinct  sequences 
#>  [>] min/max sequence lengths: 70/70
#>  [>] computing distances using the HAM metric
#>  [>] elapsed time: 0.047 secs
mvad.tree <- seqtree(mvad.seq ~ male + Grammar + funemp + gcse5eq,
                     data = mvad, diss = mvad.diss, R = 100, max.depth = 3)

# Tree with state distribution plots
# (similar to TraMineR::seqtreedisplay, which requires GraphViz)
ggseqtreeplot(mvad.tree)


# \donttest{
# Tree with index plots (only shown for the terminal nodes)
ggseqtreeplot(mvad.tree, type = "i", only.leaf = TRUE)


# Tree with mean time plots using a common y-axis for all nodes
ggseqtreeplot(mvad.tree, type = "mt", common.y = TRUE)


# make use of ggplot functions for modifying the plot
ggseqtreeplot(mvad.tree) +
  labs(title = "Regression tree of school-to-work trajectories") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")


# adjust all node plots: x-axis labels and size of split information
ggseqtreeplot(mvad.tree,
              node.layers = list(
                scale_x_discrete(breaks = c(1, 13, 25, 37, 49, 61),
                                 labels = 1993:1998),
                theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 6))
              ))


# layout similar to TraMineR::seqtreedisplay: legend in the upper left
# and global quality in the upper right corner
ggseqtreeplot(mvad.tree, quality.multiline = TRUE) +
  theme(plot.tag.location = "panel",
        plot.tag.position = c(1, 1),
        plot.tag = element_text(hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0, 1),
        legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.direction = "vertical")

# }
